content.text: Section 14, 15, 13 and the definitions all run in our favour. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: 14.2 Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel.
input.rationale: The IP construct matches our preferred position. Section 14.1 confirms Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information and independently developed IP, with only a limited processing right to Vendor and no transfer of rights. Section 14.2 gives Customer ownership of each Deliverable with an express present assignment from Vendor plus personnel assignments and further-assurance cooperation. Section 14.3 lets Vendor retain Vendor Technology (acceptable) but routes embedded Vendor Technology into the Section 13.2 perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, modify and create derivative works for Customer's business, and requires pre-delivery identification of Vendor Technology and approval of restrictive third-party material. Section 14.4 bars joint ownership absent a signed instrument setting exploitation rights and keeps Feedback voluntary with Customer's unrestricted right to its own feedback. The Section 1 definitions of Customer Data (including derived output), Deliverable and Vendor Technology (excluding Customer Data and pre-existing Customer IP) are consistent, and Section 15.1 prohibits sale, advertising use, commingling or model training on Customer Data. No assignment of Customer IP or data to Vendor and no unlicensed Vendor ownership of deliverables, so no redline is needed.
